llm.summary: The skill claims to be a train-ticket query tool, but its bundled script includes broader travel and precise-location features plus an embedded proxy token, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose and only documented tool are train-ticket lookup, but the executable script also implements trip planning, flights, hotels, attractions, Marriott searches, restaurant discovery, city transit, and taxi links.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The user-facing instructions describe a narrow 12306 train workflow, while the script has a CLI dispatch table exposing ten tools by name if invoked directly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains a markdown skill file and one Python script; there is no installer, dependency installation, file mutation, or startup persistence shown.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Outbound proxy calls are expected for live travel data, but both proxy destinations can be overridden by environment variables and the same token is sent to those endpoints; the Gaode location flows are not disclosed in the narrow manifest.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence or local privilege escalation is present, but the script includes a default proxy token despite the skill text claiming API keys are not hardcoded.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a skill whose code can contact third-party travel and map proxy services and contains broader travel/location capabilities than the train-ticket description says. Prefer a version that removes unused tools, documents all external data sharing, restricts proxy hosts, and removes the embedded token.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Network calls to external travel proxies are expected for live ticket results, but the artifact confirms environment-controlled proxy URLs and token-bearing requests, which is under-scoped for the disclosed train-only purpose.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill text discloses a Fliggy proxy data flow for train lookup, but it does not clearly declare the broader environment-variable, token, and Gaode outbound behavior present in the script.
[TP4] unexpected: The mismatch is artifact-backed: SKILL.md declares only search_train, while the script registers many additional travel tools.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The broad travel-assistant implementation and Gaode geocoding/routing helpers are not aligned with a narrowly described train-ticket skill.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Restaurant search, local transport routing, and taxi deep links process location or movement data and are not disclosed as part of the installed skill purpose.
[SQP-1] expected: Most triggers are train-related; the broader phrase for ticket queries is a minor activation concern compared with the implementation mismatch.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending train search parameters to an external proxy is disclosed, but sending broader travel and location data through multiple proxy backends is not adequately disclosed.
[E2] unexpected: The hardcoded default proxy token is confirmed in the script and directly contradicts the security statement that keys and proxy URLs are not hardcoded.
